photoperiod-night-length.alt: Four 24-hour cycles drawn as bars of light and dark, with the result for a short-day plant and a long-day plant. With 8 hours of light and 16 of dark, the short-day plant flowers and the long-day plant does not. With 16 hours of light and 8 of dark, the long-day plant flowers and the short-day plant does not. When the 16-hour night is split in half by a 5-minute flash of red light, the long-day plant flowers and the short-day plant does not. When a far-red flash follows the red one, the short-day plant flowers again and the long-day plant does not. Both plants have a critical night length of about 11 hours; what counts is the longest stretch of unbroken dark.
